text: Two fair dice are thrown together. The probability that the sum of the numbers on the top faces is 9 is
answer: Correct option: a) 1/9. Sum 9 occurs in (3,6),(4,5),(5,4),(6,3): 4 outcomes out of 36, so P = 4/36 = 1/9.

text: Two dice are rolled once. The probability that the difference of the numbers on them is 2 is
answer: Correct option: c) 2/9. Favourable: (1,3),(2,4),(3,5),(4,6) and their reverses = 8 outcomes. P = 8/36 = 2/9.

text: A die is thrown once. The probability of getting a prime number is
answer: Correct option: b) 1/2. Primes on a die: 2, 3, 5, so 3 favourable out of 6. P = 3/6 = 1/2 (1 is not prime).

text: Two dice are thrown together. The probability that the sum of the numbers is either 5 or 11 is
answer: Correct option: d) 1/6. Sum 5: (1,4),(2,3),(3,2),(4,1) = 4 outcomes; sum 11: (5,6),(6,5) = 2 outcomes. Total 6, so P = 6/36 = 1/6.

text: A card is drawn at random from cards numbered 1 to 30. The probability that the number on it is a multiple of 7 is
answer: Correct option: c) 2/15. Multiples of 7: 7, 14, 21, 28, i.e. 4 out of 30. P = 4/30 = 2/15.

text: Cards numbered 2, 3, 4, ..., 21 are placed in a box and one card is drawn at random. The probability that the number is prime is
answer: Correct option: b) 2/5. There are 20 cards. Primes: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19 = 8. P = 8/20 = 2/5.

text: The probability of winning a raffle is 2/25. If 400 tickets were sold in all, the number of tickets bought by one person who has this winning probability is
answer: Correct option: a) 32. P(win) = tickets bought / 400 = 2/25, so tickets bought = 400 × 2/25 = 32.

text: A two-digit number is chosen at random. The probability that it is divisible by 5 is
answer: Correct option: d) 1/5. Two-digit numbers: 10 to 99, so 90 in all. Multiples of 5: 10, 15, ..., 95 = 18. P = 18/90 = 1/5.

text: If the probability that an event E happens is 0.37, then the probability that E does not happen is
answer: Correct option: b) 0.63. P(not E) = 1 − P(E) = 1 − 0.37 = 0.63.

text: For an event E, P(E) = 2x and P(not E) = x + 0.4. The value of P(E) is
answer: Correct option: b) 0.4. P(E) + P(not E) = 1, so 3x + 0.4 = 1, x = 0.2. Hence P(E) = 2x = 0.4.

text: If P(not E) is three times P(E), then P(E) is
answer: Correct option: c) 1/4. Let P(E) = p. Then p + 3p = 1, so p = 1/4.

text: Which of the following can be the probability of an event?
answer: Correct option: d) 11/12. A probability must lie between 0 and 1 inclusive. Only 11/12 does; 4/3 and 1.05 exceed 1 and −0.25 is negative.

text: In a group of 40 persons, 9 cannot swim. One person is chosen at random. The probability that the person can swim is
answer: Correct option: a) 31/40. Swimmers = 40 − 9 = 31. P = 31/40.

text: A bag contains 5 red, 8 white, 4 green and 3 black balls. One ball is drawn at random. The probability that it is neither white nor green is
answer: Correct option: b) 2/5. Neither white nor green means red or black: 5 + 3 = 8 out of 20 balls. P = 8/20 = 2/5.

text: A bag contains 9 red balls and some green balls. If the probability of drawing a red ball is 3/7, the number of green balls is
answer: Correct option: c) 12. Total balls n satisfy 9/n = 3/7, so n = 21. Green balls = 21 − 9 = 12.

text: A card is drawn from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. The probability that it is a red face card is
answer: Correct option: d) 3/26. Red face cards: J, Q, K of hearts and of diamonds = 6. P = 6/52 = 3/26.

text: One card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards. The probability that it is a king or a heart is
answer: Correct option: a) 4/13. Kings = 4, hearts = 13, king of hearts counted twice, so favourable = 4 + 13 − 1 = 16. P = 16/52 = 4/13.

text: Three fair coins are tossed together. The probability of getting exactly two heads is
answer: Correct option: b) 3/8. Outcomes HHT, HTH, THH give exactly two heads: 3 out of 8. P = 3/8.

text:
Assertion (A): If the probability that it rains tomorrow is 0.58, then the probability that it does not rain tomorrow is 0.42.
Reason (R): For any event E, P(E) + P(not E) = 1.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
answer: Correct option: a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A. P(not E) = 1 − 0.58 = 0.42, so A is true; R is true and is exactly the rule used.

text:
Assertion (A): The probability that a non-leap year has 53 Sundays is 2/7.
Reason (R): A non-leap year has 52 complete weeks and 1 extra day.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
answer: Correct option: d) A is false but R is true. The 1 extra day can be any of 7 weekdays, so P(53 Sundays) = 1/7, not 2/7. A is false; R is true.

text:
Assertion (A): When a fair coin is tossed once, the probability of getting a head is 1/2.
Reason (R): The probability of any event always lies between 0 and 1, both inclusive.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
answer: Correct option: b) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A. A is true (1 favourable of 2 equally likely outcomes) and R is true, but R only gives a range and does not explain the value 1/2.

text: A bag contains 3 red, 5 blue and 7 yellow balls. One ball is drawn at random. Find the probability that it is (i) blue, (ii) not yellow.
answer:
Total balls = 3 + 5 + 7 = 15.
(i) P(blue) = 5/15 = 1/3.
(ii) Balls that are not yellow = 3 + 5 = 8, so P(not yellow) = 8/15.
Answer: (i) 1/3, (ii) 8/15.

text: A bag contains 12 red and 8 blue balls. How many red balls must be added to the bag so that the probability of drawing a red ball becomes 4/5?
answer:
Let x red balls be added. Then red = 12 + x and total = 20 + x.
(12 + x)/(20 + x) = 4/5 ⇒ 60 + 5x = 80 + 4x ⇒ x = 20.
Check: 32/40 = 4/5.
Answer: 20 red balls.

text: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. Find the probability that it is (i) a red king, (ii) a spade that is not an ace.
answer:
(i) Red kings: king of hearts and king of diamonds = 2, so P = 2/52 = 1/26.
(ii) Spades = 13, of which 1 is the ace, leaving 12. P = 12/52 = 3/13.
Answer: (i) 1/26, (ii) 3/13.

text: Three coins are tossed together. Find the probability of getting (i) at most one head, (ii) all three faces the same.
answer:
Sample space has 8 outcomes: HHH, HHT, HTH, THH, HTT, THT, TTH, TTT.
(i) At most one head: TTT, HTT, THT, TTH = 4, so P = 4/8 = 1/2.
(ii) All same: HHH, TTT = 2, so P = 2/8 = 1/4.
Answer: (i) 1/2, (ii) 1/4.

text: In a class of 48 students, the probability that a randomly chosen student does not cycle to school is 7/12. Find the number of students who cycle to school.
answer:
P(cycles) = 1 − 7/12 = 5/12.
Number who cycle = 5/12 × 48 = 20.
Answer: 20 students.

text: Two dice are thrown together. Find the probability that (i) the sum of the numbers is a perfect square, (ii) the product of the numbers is 12, (iii) the numbers differ by 3.
Three coins are tossed together. Find the probability of getting (i) at least one tail, (ii) exactly two heads, (iii) more heads than tails.
answer:
Total outcomes = 8.
(i) Only HHH has no tail, so favourable = 7, P = 7/8.
(ii) HHT, HTH, THH: P = 3/8.
(iii) More heads than tails means 2 or 3 heads: 3 + 1 = 4, P = 4/8 = 1/2.
Answer: 7/8, 3/8, 1/2.

text: Discs numbered 1 to 50 are placed in a box and one is drawn at random. Find the probability that the number on it is (i) a multiple of 4, (ii) a multiple of 6, (iii) a multiple of 4 or of 6.

At a school fair, a lucky-draw box contains 60 tickets numbered 1 to 60. A visitor draws one ticket at random.
(i) Find the probability that the number on the ticket is a multiple of 10. [1]
(ii) Find the probability that the number is a perfect square. [1]
(iii) Find the probability that the number is a two-digit prime number. [2]

A parking area has 80 vehicles: 32 two-wheelers, 28 cars, 12 autorickshaws and the rest are trucks. A vehicle is picked at random to be checked.
(i) Find the probability that it is a truck. [1]
(ii) Find the probability that it is not a car. [1]
(iii) If 20 more two-wheelers enter the parking area, find the probability that a vehicle picked at random is a two-wheeler. [2]

In a game stall, a player throws two fair dice together. The stall owner announces different prizes for different results.
(i) Find the probability that the sum of the numbers is 10. [1]
(ii) Find the probability of getting a doublet (same number on both dice). [1]
(iii) Neha wins a gift if the sum is at least 10 or the dice show a doublet. Find the probability that Neha wins. [2]
